claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy in the form of a nanoscale thin film or lithographically patterned nanoribbon.
The as-deposited nanoscale alloy exhibits a broadened magneto-structural transition.
The as-deposited nanoscale alloy exhibits enhanced or pronounced hysteresis.
Limited thermal coupling at the substrate interface causes the broadened transition and enhanced hysteresis of the baseline material.
A few-nanometer Au or Cu layer will be deposited on the substrate before deposition of the HEA film.
The ultra-thin Au or Cu interfacial layer will increase thermal conductance between the HEA film and substrate.
Increased interfacial thermal conductance will improve heat removal and heat distribution during the magneto-structural transition.
Improved interfacial heat transfer will allow the material to equilibrate thermal energy more rapidly during the phase transition.
Thermal gradients broaden the magnetocaloric response in low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi-type material.
Mitigation of thermal gradients will narrow or sharpen the magneto-structural transition.
Mitigation of thermal gradients will reduce thermal hysteresis.
Relative to the unmodified as-deposited control, samples containing the Au or Cu interfacial layer will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric transition.
Relative to the unmodified as-deposited control, samples containing the Au or Cu interfacial layer will exhibit reduced hysteresis width.
Sharpening the transition and reducing hysteresis will enhance refrigerant capacity.
The proposed mechanism applies at magnetic fields ranging from tens to a few hundred Oe.
The proposed mechanism applies near room temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies to nanoscale geometries, including films a few nanometers thick and patterned nanoribbons.
Heat-transfer dynamics limit the usable cycling rate in these nanoscale systems.
The effect of the interfacial layer may depend on film microstructure and substrate interaction.
